requirements.title: Finalizable structure and array constructors are not finalized
requirements.definition: Structure constructors and array constructors of finalizable type are not finalized by virtue of being constructors.

pending.structure-constructor-not-finalized: PENDING plan: define type t with integer tag and final subroutine that appends FINAL-tag to a saved log. Call consume_scalar(t(7)) where consume_scalar has TYPE(t), INTENT(IN) dummy and checks tag 7. After the call, assert the log is still empty. A separate subroutine creates an ordinary local TYPE(t) with tag 99 and returns, proving the same final subroutine appends FINAL-99 on an event owned by 7.5.6.3.
pending.array-constructor-not-finalized: PENDING plan: with the same type and finalizer, call consume_array([t(3),t(5)]) where consume_array has TYPE(t), INTENT(IN) dummy array and checks the exact tags [3,5]. After the call, assert the log is still empty. The ordinary-local companion finalization with tag 99 is the anti-vacuity control.

requirements.oracle: The plans use INTENT(IN) dummy consumers so no local dummy finalization is expected, distinct nonzero tags, and a separately executed ordinary local finalization companion to prove the finalizer and log are live. The oracle asserts absence of constructor-finalizer records only after the constructor value has been consumed and checked.
requirements.oracle_limitation: This compatibility unit supplies a direct plan because no existing main catalogue owns the constructor-not-finalized effect as a source unit. The ordinary finalization companion remains owned by doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_6_3.json; constructor syntax and value formation remain owned by doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_10.json and doc/catalogues/array_constructors.json.
requirements.dependencies: Confirmed existing owner catalogues opened: doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_6_3.json for ordinary finalization events, doc/catalogues/derived_types_7_5_10.json for structure constructors, and doc/catalogues/array_constructors.json for array constructors.

J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF 50: the deferred-length character compatibility item lists the IOMSG= assignment, ERRMSG= assignment, internal WRITE unit assignment, and intrinsic-subroutine INTENT(OUT) argument assignment routes for which this document specifies intrinsic-assignment semantics. Existing owners confirmed on main: doc/catalogues/iomsg_specifier_12_11_6.json for IOMSG= assignment, doc/catalogues/errmsg_specifier_9_7_5.json for ERRMSG= assignment, doc/catalogues/internal_files_12_4.json S12.4-007 for an allocatable deferred-length character scalar that is the internal WRITE unit, and doc/catalogues/intrinsic_procedure_specifications_16_9_1.json S16.9.1-002 for allocatable deferred-length character scalars corresponding to intrinsic-subroutine INTENT(INOUT) or INTENT(OUT) arguments. S12.4-007 covers the internal-WRITE unit case; its concrete already-allocated plan is `character(:), allocatable :: s; s = 'abcdefgh'; write(s,'(A)') 'xy'`, then assert `LEN(s) == 2` and `s == 'xy'`, because 12.4 p2 says an allocatable deferred-length character scalar internal file is assigned the characters written by intrinsic assignment and allocated or reallocated to have length equal to the number of characters written if necessary; blank-filling any unwritten portion applies only otherwise. S16.9.1-002 covers the intrinsic-subroutine argument case with both value and length assertions.

The sentence says this document permits SYSTEM_CLOCK to use two or more clocks with characteristics based on argument type and kind. Existing owner confirmed: doc/catalogues/system_clock_16_9_202.json, S16.9.202-009 (argument characteristics select among multiple clocks) and S16.9.202-010 (clock-selection documentation recommendation).
